desert_p17_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_001.text: Light reached the inner floor before the party did. It entered through the high slit and made a narrow bar against the threshold, then shifted a little as the morning advanced. Gao had brought a watch from her issued survey kit and wrote the observation time beside the mark. The mason rechecked the permitted entry strip and the approach before anyone entered. The cart shelf remained within yesterday's assessed margin at dawn. At camp, the drivers fed the four mules from the fodder sacks purchased with the nine-day provisions in Bitter Wells, counting actual remaining feed as well as water.

desert_p17_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_002.text: The third field day began with ordinary preparations that gave it room to change. The household bridge observer had checked the low crossing before the three gardeners went out. Its boards were sound, the visible current no higher than the previous evening's last check. The older sister carried a covered food basket; her niece and the young worker took lighter tools for the wall cap. The observer stayed on the village side. They were not leaving against a known closure. Bao saw the niece keep the heavier stone tongs with the nephew and was pleased she had accepted yesterday's advice.

desert_p17_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_003.text: A quiet morning made the upper garden look like work that might actually be finished. Across it, clouds remained banked beyond the northern hills. Inside the relay, the conservator first checked the supported fragment and the failed box without moving either quickly. Overnight conditions had changed little within the sheltered room. The original fragment remained secured in the dry custody box, with its transcription in Du's separate folder. She could now support the near portion of the collapsed lid, enough to inspect the top layer without flexing it. Yue held the clean modern board as directed.

desert_p17_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_004.text: Du waited outside the entry line until he was asked to identify a heading. The room had taught him a new way to stand: interested, breathing, and far enough from a page that his interest did not touch it. The first top sheet bore a transfer heading, not a grand name. Its list referred to receiving packets, household balances and damaged work records. Several entries were complete enough to read in place. Gao copied them literally while Du identified the known gate codes. One code led to the lower exchange's northern register.

desert_p17_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_005.text: Another belonged to a district room in Bitter Wells. The relay's missing sequence had been divided rather than vanished whole. The conservator could not yet lift the sheet safely from the material beneath it. A transcription of what could be seen would do the immediate work. Du looked almost happy to have a next place to ask instead of a final answer to declare.

desert_p17_006.speaker: du_she
desert_p17_006.text: There. The household packet was sent south before the storm-delayed works bundle. I had treated both as the same transfer because the clean summary used one line. The receiving number belongs to the municipal room, not my office. We can ask for it. The fragment's old balance is not the whole account, and the family receipt may have a later settlement beside that number. That could support a claim, or change it, or show it was already paid. I want the file found regardless.

desert_p17_007.speaker: du_she
desert_p17_007.text: The living households deserve the actual sequence more than I deserve a pleasant confirmation of my first correction.

desert_p17_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_008.text: The conservator recorded the top sheet's condition and the precise visible entries. The remainder stayed beneath the supported lid. She proposed no hurried removal of the whole box; the current handling arrangement could preserve the exposed near portion while the district decided on a better-funded conservation visit. Gao accepted the limitation, though she wanted the drainage grades farther down. The mason asked about the plaster pegs they had noticed. The room's floor carried a worn line beneath the light bar. He cleared a loose grain from it with the plain brush, then stopped when the conservator identified pigment.

desert_p17_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_009.text: The line had to be examined without scrubbing away the very thing they hoped to understand. Gao shifted her viewing shade and could see a series of small ruled divisions on the wall beside the light's edge. They were not a hidden door instruction. An old worker had marked different positions of daylight, likely for the room's sorting tasks and seasonal observations. The retained inventory mentioned a light shelf near the datum board. Its wording fitted the visible holes, where a thin screen or plate might once have stood.

desert_p17_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_010.text: Nothing in the discovery gave them the old grade without further comparison. Yue drew the holes, the surviving divisions and the current light bar as separate observed things. She resisted the temptation to make her drawing prettier by restoring missing lines. The nephew looked at the ruled wall and remembered his grandfather calling the room the morning counter. He had thought that meant somebody counted sacks there before breakfast. Du wrote the local phrase beside the inventory term. Both could be right. The room had measured goods and organised work in daylight before the market day warmed.

desert_p17_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_011.text: Gao explained how the high slit reduced glare at one shelf while illuminating the floor reference. The architecture was ingenious within ordinary materials. Yue preferred it to the town's magic palace, though she suspected the bun seller would disagree. A room designed by tired people wanting reliable morning light had a kind of wonder she could use.

desert_p17_012.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p17_012.text: The sunlight tells us where the opening puts light today, at this time and season. It does not restore an old survey by itself. For that we need the reference board, its stated method and the later changes to the floor. But the arrangement explains why the inventory cared about this slit. It also gives us a way to describe the room without inventing a buried instrument nobody has found. I like it. I would have liked to know its maker. Whoever they were, they understood that people make fewer mistakes when they can see the line they are reading.

desert_p17_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_013.text: A small scratched outline beneath the shelf resembled the narrowing outside. The mason identified it as a plan carved shallowly into a sound stone facing, not a structural cut. Gao compared its gate positions with the visible current channel. One branch in the old plan bypassed the spill throat to a low seasonal settling ground. The modern trace showed only the main run. The branch might be buried, blocked or still open; the carving alone could not tell them which. The nephew knew a damp hollow in that direction where children were forbidden after rain.

desert_p17_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_014.text: He had never thought it an old work site. The party now had another outside observation to make before anyone called the spill throat the valley's only outlet. They found the damp hollow from the safe upper bank. Its approach was covered by silt and reeds, with a partial stone lip visible where water had recently washed dust away. The mason did not clear it under live flow. Gao measured what could be observed and drew the connection as a possible old bypass pending inspection.

desert_p17_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_015.text: The household representatives wanted it included in the urgent account because it lay near a lower garden boundary. The younger representative who had hoped for easy irrigation now looked less eager. Water could give a garden a season and take its ground in an afternoon. He began moving his stored seed sacks to the upper compound before anyone ordered him to. From the well court, Bao checked the source's current appearance with the keeper. The morning draw remained ordinary, but the channel was closer to the lower lining's outer bank than on the previous day.

desert_p17_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_016.text: She asked the keeper to retain a fresh control sample and repeat the visible inspection if the flow rose. The service cisterns still held their own hundred litres of treated reserve, lids sound and taps clear, with three hundred litres of free capacity unchanged. No caravan water had entered them. The keeper said he disliked how often spare capacity was becoming a subject. Bao said she hoped it would remain merely a subject. Neither treated hope as an inspection result. Yue carried the copied transfer number to Tuo at the upper turn.

desert_p17_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_017.text: The guide read it once, then looked toward the well court where the older keeper stood. She said Du would have to explain it carefully to the family: an old receipt becoming worth checking was not the same as money being due tomorrow. Yue agreed. Tuo asked whether the room had rewarded all Du's waiting. Yue said it had given him another office. The guide laughed so suddenly that a bird left the nearby ledge. She said that was a proper ending for a mapmaker's treasure hunt.

desert_p17_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_018.text: Yue was pleased enough to keep the phrase for him at supper, if supper allowed jokes. The conservator wanted the room's exposed papers secured before the day's wind grew. She had sufficient support material for the one fragment and the top-sheet observation, less for a full box transfer. She prepared a clean protective cover that did not trap damp against the old fibres, then secured it within the sound near shelf arrangement. The district custody record would name what remained and the condition in which the party left it. Du asked whether the window should be blocked.

desert_p17_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_019.text: She said its existing ventilation mattered and could not be altered casually. The shutter could close to the tested safe angle without scraping the protection. The mason checked that movement with her watching. At the end of the morning, the current warning and old plan lay on Gao's drawing board together. The old bypass gave a physical reason to ask about a garden hollow; the current levels gave a reason to ask now.

desert_p17_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_020.text: Du looked at the two pages and admitted that his earlier public sheet would have sent everybody to inspect the named gate while missing the unnamed ground beside it. Gao said hers might have done the same before the carving and nephew's account. Their corrections no longer belonged to a contest over whose map had first been wrong. Yue carried both pages to the household representatives, who cared more about which path their children should use that afternoon. The well keeper's sister called across from the high garden strip. The wall cap was nearly finished.

desert_p17_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_021.text: She wanted the nephew to bring a second basket when he came for the tools. He answered that he would wait for the next bridge check. She lifted her hand in agreement and returned to sorting bulbs with the niece. The young worker sat in the shade writing his course enquiry more neatly on the spare paper. It was the last entirely ordinary picture Yue saw across that cut. The older woman's yellow cloth was bright against pale stone, and nothing about brightness suggested that it would become a rescue marker before the day ended.

desert_p17_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_022.text: The change began as a sound. Water below the relay court acquired a lower, fuller noise, as though the valley had taken a deep breath out of sight. The nephew stopped talking. Gao went to the same stable observation mark used that morning and found the level climbing visibly. Darker flow carried fresh twigs from upstream. Rain had fallen across the northern catchment while the local court remained almost dry. The branch obstruction reduced the receiving throat's passage. The household observer called from the low crossing and began bringing people back toward the upper paths.

desert_p17_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_023.text: The warning was no longer a page preparing for a possibility. It was a voice changing where bodies stood.

desert_p17_024.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p17_024.text: All indoor handling stops. Close the supported cover as planned, take the secured fragment and modern copies under their recorded custody, and leave the box where it is. Mason, check the return approach from the safe side. Drivers stay with the carts until we know its condition. Tuo remains on firm upper ground. Bao, the well court and crossing may need you. Yue, carry the household warning first, then return by the high path. We are not finishing the old table before we look at the current water. Everybody knows what they are leaving.

desert_p17_025.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p17_025.text: Let us be equally clear about where we are going.

desert_p17_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_026.text: Yue ran only on the broad sound path where running was safe, then slowed at the turn. She delivered the warning to the representatives while the nephew checked the bridge from above. The water had reached its lower timber supports. The older sister and the two younger workers were still on the high garden strip beyond it. The strip itself remained above the flow; the bridge was becoming the vulnerable part. The observer shouted for them to stay off the crossing. They answered.

desert_p17_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_027.text: The older woman had already gathered the basket, and the niece stood beside her with one hand at the sore shoulder. They were separated, not yet swept away. There was time to choose a better way. The bridge failed at its far footing before anyone could cross. A timber end shifted, the remaining boards turned, and the current took the loose span against the stone lip downstream. The sound was sharp, then vanished into the water's larger noise. The three workers stepped back onto higher ground.

desert_p17_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_028.text: The older woman stumbled while turning with the basket and landed awkwardly beside the garden wall. Her niece knelt at once. Across the cut, Bao saw the fall but could not diagnose it from a distance. She called for them to keep the woman still unless the water threatened that exact place. The high strip had room above the flow. Panic did not need to supply the missing bridge. The household nephew wanted to throw a rope directly across. The mason stopped him long enough to examine the line.

desert_p17_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_029.text: The current below was fast, the bank edges soft, and the available anchor on their side was a garden post meant for vines. A rope pulled from there could take the post and a person with it. The mason knew an alternative possibility from his morning view: an upper rock saddle joined the garden's far end to a dry spur beyond the relay. It needed direct inspection. The nephew knew the local path to that saddle. They went together from firm ground while Bao kept communication across the cut and the drivers secured the waiting carts.

desert_p17_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_030.text: Du had packed the transcription before leaving the room, but left a modern ruler on the shelf. He looked back toward the court and then stayed where Gao had put him. The ruler could remain. That small restraint cost him surprisingly much after so many hours of careful work. He took the conservator's dry box to the designated safe shoulder and held it there while she checked its straps. The supported fragment was inside, inventoried; the rest of the old box remained protected in place. Their testimony would be partial.

desert_p17_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_031.text: Across the water, the older sister raised one hand to show she was awake. The gesture gave the partial testimony a very clear companion.

desert_p17_032.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p17_032.text: Tell me where it hurts, using your own hand if you can. Do not let the young man pull you upright to test it. There, your lower leg and hip. Can you move the foot gently without sharp pain? Stop if it hurts. Good, stop now; I have seen enough from here. Keep the cloak under your head, and move the basket away from your body. The water is below your present shelf. We are finding an approach from higher ground. I will come when that route is cleared.

desert_p17_033.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p17_033.text: Until then, your task is to stay where you can answer me, not to prove that you can stand.

desert_p17_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_034.text: The niece translated the clinician's gestures for her aunt, though both could hear the words. The young worker moved the basket and placed his own jacket beneath the older woman's head at Bao's direction. His course enquiry went back into the dry pouch before he knelt; Yue saw that tiny preservation and liked him for it. The niece reported her shoulder pain had increased when she caught the aunt, but she could move safely on foot. The young man had cut one finger on the wall edge, bleeding but controlled under his cloth. Those reports would need examination.

desert_p17_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_035.text: For now they made three actual people out of the alarming shape across the water. The well keeper closed the ordinary draw when surface water reached a suspect outer lining point. Bao agreed it should remain closed pending a proper source review; boiling uncertain flood-affected water would not solve every possible hazard. The community's existing hundred litres of treated reserve remained protected in the covered cisterns. Representatives began distributing from that limited stock under their own count while households brought their own clean stored supplies into the common picture. None of that water became the caravan's.

desert_p17_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_036.text: Yue saw the keeper tie the well rope high and hang a closure board beneath it. His irritation had become work, precise enough to keep fear from swallowing the whole court. At the cart approach, the monitored lip had changed beyond the mason's morning assessed margin. Both carts were still on the safe upper shoulder, before that damaged point. They could remain there temporarily, but their original loaded crossing plan was withdrawn. A wider upper line existed nearby; it needed a separate assessment and limited stabilization before any cart used it.

desert_p17_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_037.text: The drivers measured their current tank draws and checked the load records. Gao put the old route sheet face down. A remembered safe way could become unsafe while the people who remembered it still stood beside it. The new line would need to earn its own passage. Tuo kept the common shoulder clear as villagers came up from the lower gardens. Her seated position had become a place where people could ask which path was open. She used Gao's current warning, not her old winter confidence. Children brought hoes, a startled hen and a bowl whose owner nobody knew.

desert_p17_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_038.text: Tuo sent the children onward with an adult representative and kept the hoes out of the wheel line. The hen escaped before a negotiation could begin and ran uphill, sensibly. Yue returned with the well closure account, breathing hard from the permitted fast sections of the path. Tuo gave her the next task in a voice that made it sound possible. The mason and nephew returned with a usable high foot approach. It joined the garden's upper end by a broad rock saddle, dry and stable under observed pedestrian conditions.

desert_p17_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_039.text: The narrow initial climb required single passage with no equipment piled at its edge; beyond it a stretcher could pass within the sound width they had measured. The route was longer than the broken bridge and did not touch the active current. Bao took her kit and the checked folding stretcher loaned by the town clinic for this expedition. Its carrier and weight rating were recorded with her medical hire. The drivers would help after securing their carts. Yue carried light flags to show the return line, staying clear of the exposed side.

desert_p17_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_040.text: Du offered to carry the stretcher and Bao asked him instead to keep the dry documents with the conservator. His balance on rough ground was less reliable than the drivers', and the supported papers still mattered. He accepted without a theatrical declaration of uselessness. Gao accompanied the mason to mark the wider return approach while the nephew led the clinical group toward the garden. The party divided its work with the households: residents watched the water and moved local stores, drivers helped carry, the clinician examined, surveyors checked ground. No new person arrived to solve it from nowhere.

desert_p17_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_041.text: Everyone already there found a task with a limit and a reason. From the cleared high saddle, Yue could see the garden strip below the rock's shoulder. The older sister lay beneath the young worker's jacket, her yellow cloth tucked away from her eyes. The niece looked up when Bao arrived and began talking so fast the clinician held out a quiet hand. The young man showed his bandaged finger, then pointed at the older woman's leg. Bao knelt beside her. The mason checked the stretcher's standing place, broad and firm, while the drivers waited for instructions.

desert_p17_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_042.text: Yue set the last light flag on the safe side of the route. The ruined bridge was out of sight. For the first time since its timber moved, the three workers no longer looked unreachable. Bao's examination found an older woman in pain, alert but shaken, with a lower-leg injury needing support and fuller imaging in town; no confident fracture label could be supplied here. Her circulation and sensation required monitoring during transfer. The niece's shoulder needed rest from lifting, and the young man's finger required cleaning, dressing and later review.

desert_p17_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_043.text: Both could walk the cleared high route without adding to the carried load. They had their own food and remaining skins, which Bao checked and supplemented from the recorded medical draw where necessary. The older woman tried to apologise for her basket. Bao told her that onions were not the patient. The woman laughed once, painfully but unmistakably alive. The clinician stabilized the older woman's leg with the compact field supports, protected her from the ground and organised a coordinated lift into the rated stretcher.

desert_p17_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_044.text: The mason, both drivers and the nephew carried at their assigned handles, keeping the load low and stopping at firm widening points. Bao walked beside them to monitor the patient. Yue carried the light kit and showed the flagged turns; Gao kept the far end of the route clear. The conservator and Du watched from the safe shoulder with the documents. The return was slow, physical work. It used no cultivated force to make an uncertain stance feel certain, and no promise that pain meant the body would recover on schedule.

desert_p17_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_045.text: At the first broad rest, the older woman asked whether her onions had survived. The young worker held up the basket, looking offended on their behalf. She closed her eyes and said he could take them to his mother if they all reached the court. Bao checked the supported leg again and asked the carriers to wait while the patient drank a measured small portion appropriate to her condition. The woman did not try to hurry them. Pain had narrowed her usual authority to a voice and a raised finger.

desert_p17_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_046.text: She used both to tell the niece to stop touching the sore shoulder. Even carried through an emergency, she could remain somebody's aunt. The rock saddle had a patch wide enough for the stretcher to stand on all its supports. Beyond it the path descended by firm shallow steps. The mason took the near handle there, the drivers the outer ones, the nephew the remaining corner, keeping the patient level through the turn. Yue carried the basket and medical kit rather than offer a fifth incompatible hand. She could hear each man's breath change under the load.

desert_p17_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_047.text: Her own breath wanted to hurry. She made it ordinary and watched the next safe standing place. The stage she had earned did not remove the usefulness of seeing where a tired foot would land. At the communal shoulder, the household representatives had cleared a treatment place under a sound shade cover. Bao received the stretcher there and repeated the checks she could make without pretending to have town equipment. The older woman's pain needed ongoing care and fuller assessment; she should be transferred to the municipal clinic rather than left to manage a doubtful injury in the hollow.

desert_p17_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_048.text: The niece's shoulder and young man's finger also warranted review, though both remained able to walk. Their households were consulted. The party could take three patients if the cart plan and return stock supported it. It was a medical proposal with practical questions still attached, not a rescue declared finished because people had reached dry ground.

desert_p17_049.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p17_049.text: I want her in the clinic where the injury can be assessed fully. I can support and monitor her on the road, but I cannot turn this field kit into the examination room she needs. The two younger workers can walk the firm route with rest and no load on the injured side. I will review them before departure and again at the stops. If either condition changes, we change the transport plan. I also need the old woman's own agreement while she is alert, and a household contact who knows where we are taking her.

desert_p17_050.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p17_050.text: Nobody should have to discover a relative's destination by reading our route warning.

desert_p17_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_051.text: The well keeper's older sister agreed after asking whether the clinic charged on arrival. Bao explained the municipal transfer provision and the later matters the household could ask about directly. Han's return fund covered the party's emergency transport costs within its stated terms, not every future treatment bill in the district. The household representative wrote the woman's contact and arranged a real market message to her family in town. The niece would travel as a patient and companion, with no lifting expected. The young worker wanted to go for his finger and feared missing the wall work.

desert_p17_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_052.text: His uncle said the wall cap could wait for a hand that healed properly. Gao counted the changed party aloud: their original nine and the three local patients, twelve adults, still four mules and two carts. The young man carried his own remaining skin and meal wrapper, neither credited as caravan stock until Bao had checked what could actually be used. For the common forecast she assumed the team would provide the needed daily water. It was safer than making the return depend on a half-full local skin nobody had measured.

desert_p17_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_053.text: The extra field drinks and treatment were entered in that day's actual withdrawals. The numbers acquired faces quickly now: a bandaged finger, a yellow cloth, a woman refusing to let her aunt apologise for being hurt. The well court filled with neighbours moving ordinary things uphill. A cooking pot, two sacks of grain, the hen finally recaptured, a child's sleeping mat. Most households remained in sound upper compounds; lower garden stores and one exposed shed were cleared as a precaution. This was no empty ruin producing three isolated victims.

desert_p17_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_054.text: It was a community responding to a changed source and cut paths. The first driver helped a woman move her grain without putting it into expedition cargo. Du carried the loose public drawings to the common notice board. Yue moved the child's mat to a clean dry wall at its owner's direction, then returned to the patients. The foreman's runner reached the upper shoulder in midafternoon by the quarry's high foot route. He had left at dawn after the urgent message arrived the previous day.

desert_p17_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_055.text: The diverted quarry branch had been reduced to its safe limited setting, with further work dependent on downstream levels. His signed note also warned of reported northern catchment rain. He had not brought a miraculous end to the valley's flow. The larger stream was already arriving through the older runnels. Gao read the note to the household representatives, recorded its actual scope and sent the runner to a resident who could show him the changed throat from a safe position. He carried his own travel water and would return after observing the current condition.

desert_p17_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_056.text: The keeper wanted to know when the well could reopen. Bao could give him no hour. Surface water had reached a suspect point; the lining and fresh source would need inspection and appropriate testing after conditions settled. The existing treated hundred litres were finite and already being distributed carefully alongside households' own clean stores. The keeper stared at the two cistern lids. Their free three hundred litres had stopped being reassuring spare space and become a measure of what they lacked. He did not demand the caravan's water. He asked whether the route authority could bring supply tomorrow.

desert_p17_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_057.text: The runner could carry the request. Nobody present could make tomorrow's vehicle exist by promising it. At the new upper line, the mason found sound rock beneath a shallow loose approach. It could be stabilized for a restricted light crossing with the rated cribbing and boards they had brought, within a gross limit lower than the carts' current travelling loads. The drivers inspected the turning geometry and braking line with him. Some heavy field equipment could remain in the household store; water weight was the other large adjustable load. Gao opened the current book.

desert_p17_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_058.text: After the day's total forecast and actual medical additions, they would have enough for the two-day return with twelve people if they transferred a bounded amount, but not enough for an optional extra research day without drawing deeply into protected essentials.

desert_p17_059.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p17_059.text: There is a possible load plan, but I want it checked by both drivers and the mason before anybody opens a tank. We can leave heavy inspection cargo under a signed local inventory. The first cart can be lightened for the patient carriage. The community cisterns have three hundred litres of actual clean free capacity established yesterday and rechecked today. That would be a transfer, not water disappearing and not water we still count on the road. We must keep enough to get twelve adults and four mules home with the remaining contingency.

desert_p17_060.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p17_060.text: I will calculate from actual draws, then you can tell me where the plan fails.

desert_p17_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_061.text: Du looked toward the relay's sheltered inner wall. The box might hold the old drainage grades and household transfer detail still unread. A further day could give the conservator time, if the water fell and the approach remained accessible. He could feel the words if and might multiplying in his mouth. He asked whether he and the conservator could stay behind with a local household while the patients left. The conservator asked what funded their return, supplied them safely, protected the records work and brought qualified access if the site changed again. He had answers for none of those questions.

desert_p17_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_062.text: His desire had become an unfunded expedition of two, hidden inside a supposedly simple request.

desert_p17_063.speaker: du_she
desert_p17_063.text: I wanted to stay because leaving feels like admitting that I have come too late twice. Once when the office closed, and again when I finally understood what I needed from it. That is not the same as a good reason to use the household's water or ask you to wait for me. I will leave with the party. Put the box's condition and unread portion in the report. I can help find the southern packet first.

desert_p17_064.speaker: du_she
desert_p17_064.text: If there is to be a return conservation visit, I will seek money for an actual visit, not borrow a day from people whose well is closed and call it dedication.

desert_p17_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_065.text: The conservator accepted the decision without rewarding it as heroism. She needed him useful in town, where his source knowledge could help locate the receiving number. She also needed payment for the full field work even though the box would remain partly unread. Du assured her of that, then looked embarrassed that she had needed to ask. Gao confirmed it in the common hire account. Partial findings were still findings; emergency interruption did not turn a professional's days into a hobby. Yue watched the entry acquire its clean line.

desert_p17_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_066.text: The old papers would now have a future proposed in a funded place, rather than a dramatic present no one could safely finish. The older patient woke from a short doze and saw Du standing near the stretcher. She asked whether her grandmother's receipt had helped. He told her it had given them a useful comparison and that a later packet should be sought in town. He did not say she had recovered a fortune. She laughed at the very idea, then asked him to find the packet anyway. Her grandmother had contributed because the well served neighbours.

desert_p17_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_067.text: If the account showed the contribution settled, she wanted to know how. If it showed it still credited, she wanted the living household to be heard. Either truth would be better than an office calling all of it district provision. Tuo listened from her supported chair and watched Du answer. After the woman slept again, the guide told him he had said what he knew before reaching for what he wished. He looked at her, startled by praise given without irony. She added that he remained exhausting. That restored his equilibrium.

desert_p17_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_068.text: Yue brought the patient a clean cloth from Bao's kit and took the used one to the separate medical wash arrangement. The ordinary handling kept her from becoming a spectator to everyone else's hard decisions. She had joined the second journey to see the valley. Seeing now included what people did when the interesting room could no longer be the centre of the day. The drivers emptied no tank while the new path was still being prepared. They placed chocks on the safe shoulder and reviewed the documented empty cart weights, remaining cargo and conservative passenger allowances.

desert_p17_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_069.text: The first vehicle's service deck could receive the clinic stretcher only after its heavy crates were moved; the entire carrier footprint and rated restraint points had to be clear. The second needed Tuo's seated place protected. Both axle distributions mattered as well as total mass. The mason listened to the driver calculations and adjusted the cribbing plan around the actual wheels. Their emergency craft consisted of ordinary things becoming very specific, one strap and one board at a time. The young worker helped write the inventory for equipment proposed to remain in the community's dry shed.

desert_p17_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_070.text: He used his uninjured hand and complained that the characters looked like caterpillars. The village girl offered to copy them neatly. He said the town school might reject caterpillars. She replied that a metal course probably had worse handwriting than he did. Yue let them argue over the modern inventory while keeping the important numbers legible. The household custodian would sign for the actual packages, and Han would arrange collection with permission after the route was safe. Nothing was being donated merely because an emergency made its ownership inconvenient. The patient transfer changed supper before it changed the carts.

desert_p17_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_071.text: The party had bought nine days of provisions for nine adults; after four days, enough remained for twelve on the planned two-day return with contingency. The mules' remaining fodder was checked separately. The households cooked their own meal from their own stores, while the three patients received the expedition's planned portions and appropriate care. Du volunteered for chopping and was put on washing spoons instead because the knife had already been through a difficult morning. Yue tasted the lentils before they were served.

desert_p17_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_072.text: There was still a little onion in them, bought yesterday from a girl whose well was now closed. At the common notice board, Gao drew the present safe paths in a broad hand. The footbridge was crossed out; the upper foot saddle remained the observed pedestrian return; the lighter cart line stayed marked pending final stabilization and load checks. The old relay route did not vanish from the sheet, but its current access was suspended. Residents gathered close enough to see, correcting a garden name and asking where the well request stood.

desert_p17_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_073.text: Gao took the corrections before sealing the dated copy. A map made under urgency could still use the words of people who would remain beside it after the cart tracks led away. The foreman's runner took the urgent supply request and receiving observations back toward the quarry before evening, while the high foot route remained open. He had seen the throat and the well closure board himself. The household representatives retained duplicate requests, and the visiting party would carry another into Bitter Wells.

desert_p17_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_074.text: These were three real routes for information, each with a person and a destination, not a guarantee that supply would arrive before dawn. The keeper began a careful common count of household clean water. People grumbled about cups and uneven contributions. They also brought what they had. A closed well had made private cupboards suddenly relevant to the court. Yue sat briefly beside the niece while Bao checked the older patient's leg. The younger woman had taken off the work sling that had aggravated her shoulder and held the arm comfortably near her side.

desert_p17_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_075.text: She asked whether the town clinic would tell her she was foolish. Yue said Bao had not called her foolish here. The niece looked at her aunt, then at the empty basket, and admitted she had tried to catch too much weight at once. Yue remembered her own sudden effort at the kiln and the weeks it had cost. She told only that part of the story. It was enough for the niece to stop treating her pain as a private disgrace. Evening found the water still high but no longer climbing at the earlier rate.

desert_p17_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_076.text: The carts remained on the safe shoulder. The mason's restricted route work was ready for final daylight inspection, and the receiving cisterns had been rechecked clean and sound. Bao had twelve travelling adults to plan for now, including three patients, with four mules unchanged. The actual day's withdrawal reached one hundred and twenty-eight litres, including the additional field drinks and treatment. Eight hundred and ten remained before any transfer: four hundred and nine in the first tank, four hundred and one in the second, protected compartments included. Fuel stood at twenty-two kilograms.

desert_p17_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_077.text: Gao wrote the figures where both drivers could see them. The older sister asked to see her yellow cloth before sleep. Yue unfolded it and found the tiny onion-skin flower she had tucked into its corner. The woman had made two, one for Yue and one for herself, then forgotten the second during the morning's work. Yue placed it on the dry patient wrapper where it would not interfere with care. The woman smiled and closed her eyes. Across the shoulder, Du put the copied transfer number in the folder he would carry home.

desert_p17_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p17_078.text: Below the willow, the empty space inside two cisterns waited for a decision the travellers could now measure. Tomorrow's road would begin with giving up part of what they had brought.
